solution: The condition \(P(X < a) = P(X > a)\) means \(a\) is the median, so \(\int_{0}^{a} 6x(1 - x)\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\). Evaluating, \(\left[3x^{2} - 2x^{3}\right]_{0}^{a} = 3a^{2} - 2a^{3} = \dfrac{1}{2}\), i.e. \(4a^{3} - 6a^{2} + 1 = 0\), which factors as \((2a - 1)(2a^{2} - 2a - 1) = 0\). The quadratic factor gives \(a = \dfrac{1 \pm \sqrt{3}}{2}\), both outside \([0, 1]\), so the only admissible root is \(a = \dfrac{1}{2}\). (This is also immediate from the symmetry of \(f\) about \(x = \dfrac{1}{2}\).)

For \(0 < x < 1\) the c.d.f. is \(F(x) = \int_{0}^{x} 3\left(1 - 2t^{2}\right)dt = \left[3t - 2t^{3}\right]_{0}^{x} = 3x - 2x^{3}\). The check \(F(1) = 3 - 2 = 1\) confirms the normalisation. Note that the stated \(f\) is not a genuine p.d.f.: although \(\int_{0}^{1} f = 1\), \(f(x) = 3\left(1 - 2x^{2}\right) < 0\) for \(x > \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) (e.g. \(f(0.9) = -1.86\)), so the density fails the non-negativity requirement; the integration asked for is nevertheless \(3x - 2x^{3}\).

The event \(\left|X\right| < 1\) is \(-1 < X < 1\), so \(P\left(\left|X\right| < 1\right) = \int_{-1}^{1} \dfrac{x^{2}}{18}\,dx = \dfrac{1}{18}\left[\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}\right]_{-1}^{1} = \dfrac{1}{18} \cdot \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{1}{27}\). (The density is valid: \(\int_{-3}^{3} \dfrac{x^{2}}{18}\,dx = 1\) and \(f \geq 0\).)

Normalisation requires \(\sum_{x=0}^{\infty} k(x + 1)5^{-x} = 1\). Using \(\sum_{x=0}^{\infty}(x + 1)r^{x} = \dfrac{1}{(1 - r)^{2}}\) with \(r = \dfrac{1}{5}\), the sum is \(\dfrac{k}{\left(\dfrac{4}{5}\right)^{2}} = \dfrac{25k}{16} = 1\), so \(k = \dfrac{16}{25}\). Hence \(P(X = 0) = k(0 + 1)5^{0} = \dfrac{16}{25}\).

Here \(X\) is binomial with \(n = 5\), \(p = \dfrac{1}{2}\), and the p.m.f. is symmetric since \({}^{5}C_{x} = {}^{5}C_{5-x}\). Therefore \(a = P(X \leq 2) = \dfrac{1 + 5 + 10}{32} = \dfrac{16}{32} = \dfrac{1}{2}\) and \(b = P(X \geq 3) = \dfrac{10 + 5 + 1}{32} = \dfrac{1}{2}\), so \(a = b\). The stem's phrase \(E(X) =\) is a misprint: the actual expectation is \(E(X) = np = \dfrac{5}{2}\), which matches none of the four options, all of which compare \(a\) and \(b\); the question intended is the comparison, whose answer is \(a = b\).

Normalisation gives \(c\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{8} + \dfrac{1}{27}\right) = c \cdot \dfrac{251}{216} = 1\), so \(c = \dfrac{216}{251}\). Then \(E(X) = \sum_{x=1}^{3} x \cdot \dfrac{c}{x^{3}} = c\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{9}\right) = c \cdot \dfrac{49}{36}\). Hence \(E(X) = \dfrac{216}{251} \cdot \dfrac{49}{36} = \dfrac{294}{251} \approx 1.1713\).

Summing the probabilities to \(1\) gives \(k + 2k + 2k + 3k + k^{2} + 2k^{2} + \left(7k^{2} + k\right) = 10k^{2} + 9k = 1\), i.e. \(10k^{2} + 9k - 1 = 0\), which factors as \((10k - 1)(k + 1) = 0\). The root \(k = -1\) is rejected because a probability cannot be negative, so \(k = \dfrac{1}{10}\).
